sources.title: Neural Evidence and Behavioural Welfare Economics: When Can Neuroeconomics Inform Policy?
sources.snippet: Neuroeconomics appears to offer welfare economics an evidential supplement, since neural data may help distinguish choices that express genuine preferences from choices distorted by addiction, framing or self-control failure. This paper asks when such evidence can legitimately inform welfare judgements for policy.
